description: Three goals: (1) reduce long-method smells in 10 production methods; (2) enforce Commands-as-thin-shells architecture — all Roslyn logic moves to src/RoslynTools/Core/<Name>Core.cs; (3) add 6 new differentiating refactoring commands (transform-parameters with new/existing class, make-static, make-instance, find-pattern, extract-method --replace-duplicates).
ralph_instructions: Architectural rule: every Command class is a thin shell — its ExecuteAsync must only load the workspace and delegate to <Name>Core.RunAsync(...). All Roslyn logic lives in src/RoslynTools/Core/<Name>Core.cs. Existing examples: MethodExtractor (called by ExtractMethodCommand), FindUnusedCore (called by FindUnusedCommand). For refactor stories: move the logic to Core first, then decompose into private helpers there. For new-command stories: ship Command + Core from the start. Verification (every story, non-negotiable): `dotnet build RoslynTools.slnx`, `dotnet test RoslynTools.sln -v minimal`, `dotnet format RoslynTools.slnx --verify-no-changes`. Do NOT skip the format check.

userStories.title: New command: transform-parameters (new class)
userStories.description: As a user, I want to extract a method's parameters into a new record (or class) and have all call sites updated, so large parameter lists become introducible parameter objects.
acceptanceCriteria: Behaviour: generates `record <ParamObj>(...)` in the same file as the target method, rewrites the method signature to take one `<ParamObj>` parameter named `args` (or similar), rewrites every call site from `Foo(a, b, c)` to `Foo(new ParamObj(a, b, c))`
Skip parameters declared with out/ref/in modifiers (fail with a clear error listing which params were skipped)
Preserve default values from the original signature in the record parameter list

Create tests/RoslynTools.Tests/TransformParametersTests.cs with [Collection("MSBuild")] covering: simple 3-param method, method with default value, method with out param (error), multi-call-site update, dry-run emits diff without writing
dotnet test RoslynTools.sln -v minimal all green
Update README.md command table and add an example invocation
userStories.notes: Mirrors the Command+Core pattern from ExtractMethodCommand + MethodExtractor. Use TestProjectBuilder for test fixtures.

userStories.title: transform-parameters — support existing class/record via --existing-type
userStories.description: As a user, I want to reuse an existing parameters class instead of always creating a new one, since this is the common real-world case (ReSharper/Eclipse cannot do this well).
acceptanceCriteria: Add --existing-type <FQN> option to TransformParametersCommand, mutually exclusive with --new-type
Validation: the existing type has matching-named properties (for classes) or record-params (for records) for every method parameter. On failure, exit 1 with a message listing the missing properties
Call-site rewrite for class: `new ExistingType { X = a, Y = b }`; for record: `new ExistingType(a, b)`
Do NOT generate a new type when --existing-type is used
Tests added to TransformParametersTests.cs: matching existing record, matching existing class, missing property (error), partial match (error), both flags passed (error)
dotnet test RoslynTools.sln -v minimal all green
userStories.notes: Depends on US-011 — touches the same Command + Core files. Key differentiator vs commercial tooling.

userStories.title: New command: find-pattern (structural AST match across solution)
userStories.description: As a user, I want to find all code locations that structurally match a given line range, so I can identify duplicated patterns even when variable/literal names differ.
acceptanceCriteria: Create src/RoslynTools/Core/PatternMatcher.cs with public API FindMatchesAsync(Solution sln, string filePath, int startLine, int endLine, string? scope) returning a list of PatternMatch records (file, line, identifierSubstitutions)
Extract the syntax subtree from the given line range (must be a sequence of StatementSyntax inside a BlockSyntax — same constraint as extract-method)
Walk the solution; find every same-length statement sequence where SyntaxKind shape matches and only identifier/literal values differ
For each match, record: file path, start line, end line, the substitution map (pattern identifier → match identifier)
Skip the pattern source itself (don't report the origin as a match)
Create tests/RoslynTools.Tests/FindPatternTests.cs covering: exact duplicate found, identifier-only-different match found, structurally-different code not matched, cross-file match, scope filter
dotnet build + dotnet test all green
userStories.notes: The key differentiator. US-016 will consume PatternMatcher.FindMatchesAsync as a library. Prefer a clean public API on PatternMatcher; the Command is just a JSON-emitting wrapper.

userStories.title: extract-method --replace-duplicates (uses find-pattern matcher)
userStories.description: As a user, I want extract-method to optionally find structurally-matching code elsewhere in the solution and replace those occurrences with calls to the newly-extracted method, consolidating duplication in one operation.
acceptanceCriteria: When flag is set: after extracting the new method, invoke PatternMatcher.FindMatchesAsync (from US-015) with the extracted body as the pattern
For each match: rewrite the matched statements to a single call to the new method, plugging in the substituted identifiers as arguments in the correct parameter order
Skip (and warn with file:line) any match where a literal would need to become a variable — i.e. the substitution map maps a parameter to a literal in the match site
Report a summary at the end: matches found, replaced, skipped (with reasons)
Existing extract-method tests continue to pass
